page.layout: One page of text, with a woodcut diagram of a sphere set between the upper paragraph and the lower paragraph; no margin notes. The digitiser's banner at the foot is left out.

main_text.l: formam latiori zonae similem, Solis Lunaeq; et
im primo motu circumducti non interualla
inter se, et primo motui congruentia, et ab aequatore
in ortum contrario motu tendunt, tum euagantur
ad Septentrionem et Meridiem, uarietate mira
latini uocant, Circulus maior, obliquus, latitudinem
habens, mobilis ad sphaerae motum cui inhaeret, ubiq; idem, sub
quo Planetae perpetuo feruntur ac de-
Aristoteles et Ptolemaeus λόξον κύκλον latini obli-ni obli-

page.notes: The Greek phrase is printed as λόξον κύκλον, and the last line reads "latini obli-" continued at the line end as "ni obli-"; the printed line ends with a hyphen, shown here as the printer set it. The diagram shows a sphere with labelled points A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, K, L and a shaded zodiac band; it is not transcribed as text. Catchword and page number are not printed.
